summary: shopcli is a standard-library-only Python 3 package in which every failure of an inventory command language comes back as one structured refusal: a code from a closed list, a message, the path of operations, the agent's own line, valid alternatives, a concept hint, and a paste-ready fix. The suggester is ordered from certain to guessed (structural namespace fact, mined redirects for rm/delete/ls/inventory, near spelling within max(1, min(3, len//3)) applied to the differing segment, cross-kind step deliberately skipped), fixes are spliced into the agent's original source so a repeat prefix and untouched arguments survive and are only offered when they bind, and Python exceptions are translated to E_HOST with the host class kept in host_name. Warnings are raised at their line, folded with a count, and everything produced before a failure is still returned.

pattern_mapping.Refusal: shopcli/refusal.py (Refusal dataclass with code, message, path, where, valid, hint, fix, host_name; to_dict), built in one place by Shop._refusal / _from_problem / _from_failure / _translate in shopcli/shop.py
pattern_mapping.Code list: shopcli/codes.py (CODES tuple, CODE_DOCS one description each, CODE_EXAMPLES one executable example per code, WARNING_CODES/WARNING_EXAMPLES); LineProblem, CommandFailure and Shop._refusal all assert the code is in CODES; exercised by tests/test_catalogue.py
pattern_mapping.Fix renderer: Shop.render_change in shopcli/shop.py: splices the replacement into parsed.source at the failing token's span (command token, option key, or option value) and returns None unless Shop._binds accepts the candidate
pattern_mapping.Suggester: shopcli/suggest.py (suggest_command, suggest_option, edit_budget, closest_name, nearest_names); order is structural fact, redirect, near spelling, then stop
pattern_mapping.Redirect table: shopcli/registry.py (Redirect dataclass, Registry._redirects per instance, validated in Registry.__init__ so a redirect to an unknown command raises ValueError 'would not bind'); the four mined names live in shopcli/commands.py REDIRECTS and are checked by tests/test_catalogue.py::RedirectCatalogueTest and tests/test_suggestions.py::RegistryTableTest
pattern_mapping.Translator: Shop._translate and Shop._host_hint in shopcli/shop.py: any exception from a command body becomes E_HOST with host_name = type(exc).__name__ and a concept hint recognized for the zero-price report.margin
pattern_mapping.Site tracker: shopcli/parsing.py: the parser supplies where = {line, source} plus Token/Argument spans, so no separate class is needed (the task's language is interpreted by our own engine, not by a host object graph) — the chapter's condition for a tracker is not met
pattern_mapping.Warning folder: shopcli/refusal.py fold_warnings (groups by code, line, message, hint and sums count), called once in Shop.run

notes_applied: Note 1 (mine redirects, refuse with a fix): rm and delete refuse with item.remove, ls with item.list, inventory with report.stock, each with a hint naming the concept and a literal fix that keeps the agent's arguments; the fix is dropped if it would not bind.

Note 2 (one fixed suggestion order, budget on the differing segment): suggest.py checks structural namespace fact, then redirect table, then Levenshtein with max(1, min(3, len//3)) per segment; 'item.ad' matches item.add while 'item.drop' stays unmatched, and tests/test_suggestions.py::OrderTest uses a custom registry where a redirect beats a near spelling and a structural fact beats both.

Note 3 (fixes are code, keep prefix and other arguments): fixes are spliced at token spans, so 'repeat 3: item.ad name=widget qty=1' fixes to 'repeat 3: item.add name=widget qty=1' and quoted values like name="red widget" survive; tests/test_fixes.py asserts exactly one token changes and everything outside it is identical.

Note 4 (one shape, one closed code list for every layer): parser LineProblem, command CommandFailure and host exceptions all become Refusal; CODES is the single vocabulary and E_HOST is the only code that fills host_name (tested code by code).

Note 5 (the path is part of the message): path is [command label, '✗ failing part'] or ['✗ name'] for unknown commands, and the label includes the repeat structure, e.g. 'repeat 2 × item.add(name=w, qty=abc)'.
Note 6 (the line is in the agent's program): where.line and where.source come from the parser, with blank lines counted so line 3 really is line 3, and the original spacing preserved.
Note 7 (warn at the line, fold repeats): item.add above qty 1000 runs and warns RANGE at its line; repeat 500 folds into one warning with count=500 (tests/test_warnings.py).

Note 8 (deliver what was produced before the failure): Shop.run keeps results and warnings accumulated before the failing line, including iterations of a repeat; tested with an E_HOST failure and with an E_NOT_FOUND after a warning.

Note 9 (one redirect table per registry, checked at load): Redirects live on the Registry instance and are validated against it; tests/test_registry.py asserts ValueError on an unknown target and tests/test_suggestions.py proves two registries do not share their tables.

Note 10 (never invent a value to complete a fix): qty=abc, qty=1.5, a missing name, a duplicate option and a near name whose options do not fit all return a hint and fix=None; placeholders appear only in hints as '<whole number>' / '<text>' (tests/test_fixes.py::NoFixTest).

Note 11 (test codes and fixes): CODE_EXAMPLES must each raise exactly their code (tests/test_catalogue.py), and every offered fix is tested for binding and for changing only the failing token (tests/test_fixes.py).
tests: 150 tests in 9 unittest modules (tests/, run with python3 -m unittest discover -s tests); last result: Ran 150 tests in 0.036s — OK, plus seven modules' doctests with 0 failures and a 6000-line random-input sweep that produces only refusals, never an exception.
chapter_feedback: The chapter was most useful as a contract: the Refusal field list and the suggest/renderFix/translate sketches translated almost line for line, and the ordered suggester plus the edit budget gave concrete, testable behaviour instead of vague 'good errors'.
Note 2's 'apply the budget to the segment that differs' was the single most valuable sentence: it is the difference between suggesting item.add for item.drop (wrong) and leaving it alone.

The chapter's code list is JavaScript-shaped (E_UNKNOWN_METHOD) while the task requires E_UNKNOWN_COMMAND; that rename is trivial but the chapter never says how its codes map onto a task's required codes, which cost a decision.

E_NAMESPACE is underspecified for a flat command language: the chapter's example is a nested member (img.mask.luminance). I had to invent the mapping (bare verb 'add' and typo'd namespace 'items.add' are structural facts; a real but different namespace such as price.list is not) and it is the least certain design choice in the build.

The chapter's own example (fix 'repeat 3: item.add name=w' when item.add also needs qty) contradicts implementation note 11's 'the fix binds' if binding is read as 'has all required options'. I resolved it by checking only the failing token's validity, so pasting can yield E_ARG_MISSING as the next repair step; a sentence in the chapter about this would help.

Nothing in the chapter covers resource limits. A huge repeat count killed the test process, which is exactly the kind of failure that escapes the pattern and returns a Python traceback; I added E_ARG_RANGE with a documented MAX_REPEAT, but the chapter says nothing about non-repairable or resource refusals.
The chapter's advice to skip the cross-kind suggestion step in a flat language was decisive and saved a misleading price.list -> item.list fix; without that paragraph I would have wired step 4 in.
